prerequisites: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electrical circuits and passive components.

learning_outcomes.text: Upon passing the exam, the student should be able to analyze and design electronic circuits and systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to electronics: analog and digital quantities.
Differential amplifier, operational amplifier (OA) and transconductance amplifier (OTA).
Configurations with OA: inverting, non-inverting, buffer.
Circuits with non-linear open-loop OAs: comparators, astable.
Bipolar and field-effect transistors: introduction, Gm.
Non-linear transfer characteristic: biasing and small-signal equivalent circuits.
Transistor circuits (CS, CD, CE, and CC).
Introduction to digital electronics: binary representation, combinational circuits, logic gates, K-maps, sequential circuits.
Laboratory exercises: review of RC and CR circuits, circuits with OAs, diode circuits, MOSFET CS, dual-stage amplifiers, combinational and sequential circuits, A/D and D/A converters.
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written question, two oral questions, and one question on the laboratory reports. Discussions during lectures and laboratory exercises are also part of the assessment. Students are required to solve numerical exercises independently, which are then corrected.
